summary: Select proportionate evaluation methods and build an evidence-quality matrix for a live programme. Explore the course and plan your next step.
lede: Outcome evidence design helps MEAL managers, evaluation specialists and programme leaders assess how a programme contributed to observed change. They learn to frame evaluation questions, test assumptions, triangulate evidence and consider alternative explanations, then select suitable contribution analysis, outcome harvesting or quasi-experimental approaches. Practical work produces an evaluation plan and evidence-quality matrix to support proportionate conclusions and decisions when time, data and budgets are constrained.
audienceIntro: This course suits professionals who commission, manage or conduct programme evaluation and need to choose methods that fit real donor-funded programme conditions.
modules: Theory of Change and Evaluation Questions
prerequisites: Working familiarity with programme results frameworks, routine monitoring data and donor-funded programme delivery is recommended. No coding or statistical software is required; quasi-experimental methods are covered at a design-selection level.
